parts.title: Campsite Reservation Form
parts.transcript: Part 1. Sandra Kemp books a campsite (Nature Park Services). Mount Laguna is in the Southern California region (1 Southern). Chooses Mountain campground (Sunrise fishing only Jun-Sep, she's going April) (2 Mountain). Tent site for peace and quiet (3 tent). Driving a truck not a car (4 truck). Licence plate QY0918 (5 QY0918). Arriving April 10th, leaving the 12th = departure 12 April (6 April 12). Small bear-proof food container, lightweight (7 small). Flower nature walk (8 flower). One-year park pass (9 one-year). Donates to the youth programme (10 youth).

parts.transcript: Part 2. Ocean Edge Hotel manager to new staff. Late because he had to finish writing the weekly report for head office (11 A). Values enthusiasm/enjoying contact with guests over qualifications (12 B). Site: 18th-c bakery, then houses, demolished mid-20th century and replaced by the hotel, so hotel opened 20th century (13 C). Staff usually stay five years (some ten) (14 B). Fastest-growing group = regulars working locally who go home at weekends (15 C). Plan: office immediately behind the desk (16 I); function room at the front, left of reception, opposite the desk (17 F); main conference room past the fountain as far as you can, doors in front (18 B); meeting room down the corridor at side of reception desk, at the end (19 H); restaurant turn left just before the fountain toward guest rooms, large room on the right (20 C).

parts.transcript: Part 3. Terence & tutor on a presentation about Ife sculptures (Nigeria, 12th-15th c). First attracted by a special display at the City Museum (21 B). Focuses on naturalistic sculptures of kings and queens = people (22 C). Financed trip via a grant from the Arts Council (23 A). Highlight = meeting a professor working on the site (24 B). Additions to sculptures part: enlarged/bigger photos (A) + extra info on the techniques/way they were made (D) (25,26 A,D). Additions to history: more on the surrounding region/countries around Nigeria (B) + the religious beliefs of the Ife people (C) (27,28 B,C). Research-in-Nigeria features to discuss: the original discovery of the sculptures (E) + the uncertainty over who made them/same person theory (B) (29,30 B,E).

parts.title: Reasons for and against urban migration
parts.transcript: Part 4. Lecture on reasons for and against urban migration. Cities cover 3% of land but produce less carbon than non-urban areas (31 carbon). Advantages: some forests would recover (32 forests); services like electricity/water more efficient; transport in the city is more environmentally friendly (33 transport); recycling - energy from methane gas from rubbish (34 rubbish); urban women start families later and are more likely to gain promotion at work (35 promotion). Downsides: possible loss of culture amongst some migrants (36 culture); higher crime rate (37 crime); poor quality of the air (38 air); increased wealth in a population leads to more energy consumption (39 wealth); citizens find the quantity of daily traffic stressful (40 traffic).
